newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland's Niinisto says confident in EMU timetable.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Niinisto says confident in EMU timetable.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Friday he was confident that the third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU) would start according to the agreed timetable.
As he arrived at a closed-door EMU-seminar, Niinisto told a Reuters reporter he expected Finland to be in the first group of countries setting up the single currency from January 1999.

"We have all possible belief in the timetable which has been agreed ... We are confident in the timetable which has been agreed many times," Niinisto said, when asked whether he thought the scheduled start of EMU might be delayed.

European Union finance ministers were unlikely to discuss the EMU timetable at their ECOFIN meeting in Brussels on Monday. "I have no reason to believe that there would be discussions (about the timetable)," he said.

The ECOFIN agenda includes the French and German EMU convergence programmes, and Niinisto said that on those "surely there will be a lot of discussion ... but not to my knowledge about the (EMU) timetable".
When asked if he thought Finland would be in the first group founding the single currency in January 1999, Niinisto said: "Yes." --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
